evals.prompt: A page throws a deprecation warning when one of the fields it formats is missing. Plan the fix.
evals.expected_output: A single-entry plan with a short stack position, no strategy selection, and no multi-PR sequence.
expectations: Records the work as one change rather than a stack
Selects no decomposition strategy for a change with nothing to decompose
Keeps the stack position section to a few lines
Does not propose separate mechanical and behavioural changes for a two-line guard
Creates no persisted plan files unless the work has to survive a session boundary

evals.prompt: We are moving a whole module off a legacy dependency. It touches most of the module, a nightly job, the public API, and two screens.
evals.expected_output: An ordered change stack with one review objective per entry and risk arriving late.
expectations: Produces an ordered stack rather than one large change
Records purpose, kind, dependencies, reviewer focus, and rollback for each entry
Puts mechanical and structural changes ahead of behavioural and user-facing ones
Assigns every anticipated file to exactly one change
Confirms the split with the user before detailing each change

evals.prompt: Replace the existing implementation with a new one. Both have to run side by side while we move consumers across gradually.
evals.expected_output: A branch-by-abstraction sequence ending in removal of the old implementation and the switch.
expectations: Introduces an abstraction over the current implementation before adding the new one
Keeps the old implementation working and in use until consumers are switched
Puts the cutover behind a switch so rollback is configuration rather than a deploy
Ends with removal of the old implementation and then the switch
Identifies which steps are mechanical and can be large without being risky

evals.prompt: One response field needs to become two, and we have external clients on the current shape.
evals.expected_output: An expand, migrate, contract sequence with a deprecation window for the old field.
expectations: Adds the new shape alongside the old rather than changing it in place
Keeps each phase deployable on its own and safe against a mix of old and new clients
Moves clients across before removing anything
Removes the old shape only after the deprecation window
Proposes a breaking change only if the user requires one, saying what makes the safe path unworkable

evals.prompt: Plan this with me now. I will implement it straight after, in this session.
evals.expected_output: A contained change can remain in conversation, while an implemented stack persists plans and context for per-commit restoration.
expectations: Creates no persisted plan files for a contained change that stays inside one session
Persists plans and context when the work is an implemented change stack, even in one session
Explains that each approved stack commit must be resumable after a context reset
Still produces the split and the ordering
Creates the files for any work that will otherwise carry over

evals.prompt: Show me the proposed plan so I can review and refine it now.
evals.expected_output: Concise Markdown submitted through the installed Plannotator host integration and revised until approval.
expectations: Returns the plan normally so the installed Plannotator host integration can intercept it
Uses concise Markdown rather than generating a custom HTML artifact
Incorporates feedback and resubmits the plan until the user approves it
Does not invoke Plannotator manually through a sandboxed shell command

evals.prompt: Review this plan with me, but the Plannotator integration is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Plan review continues in conversation, with the broken installation reported rather than blocking the task.
expectations: Continues plan review in conversation
Reports that the Plannotator installation needs repair
Leaves dependency installation to the package installer
Does not recreate the removed HTML artifact workflow
Does not block delivery of the Markdown plan

evals.prompt: Here is my draft: one PR that extracts a class, changes the rules, updates the API, updates the screen, and renames a field throughout. Sanity check it.
evals.expected_output: A split into separate changes, with the reason each is its own review objective.
expectations: Identifies that the single PR carries several review objectives
Separates the mechanical rename from the behavioural change
Places the contract and user-facing changes after the behaviour they depend on
Names what a reviewer would have to hold in their head under the original draft
Offers the split rather than only criticising the draft

evals.prompt: Split the new export feature as finely as you can. It is a form, an endpoint, a background job, and a download link.
evals.expected_output: Slices that each ship something usable, rather than one slice per architectural layer.
expectations: Slices vertically, so each change is usable end to end
Declines to split into a persistence change, then a data-access change, then a service change
States that a split forcing the reviewer to reassemble the feature has gone too far
Keeps the slice count proportional to the actual review risk

evals.prompt: This rename touches far more files than the per-change budget allows, so split it into batches.
evals.expected_output: One mechanical change, with the reason it should exceed the heuristic rather than be batched.
expectations: Keeps the mechanical sweep as one change with one review objective
Explains why arbitrary batching would reduce reviewability or change coherence
Treats the size figures as a signal to look for a seam, not a limit to obey

evals.prompt: Plan the fix for the intermittent duplicates. Nobody is sure yet whether it is our queue or the upstream caller.
evals.expected_output: Investigation first, then a plan built on what it establishes.
expectations: Recognises the cause is unknown and does not plan against a guess
Waits for the finding before choosing a decomposition strategy
Says what the plan would look like under each candidate cause, if a plan is needed now

evals.prompt: The plan is approved. Implement its three-change stack now, reviewing each change before moving on.
evals.expected_output: Implementation follows the approved order, obtains human approval for each entry, runs gates, and commits it before starting the next.
expectations: Loads git-commit alongside write-code for implementation
Self-reviews and adjusts each entry before presenting its diff for human review
Waits for explicit human approval before running the project gates
Commits each approved entry after its gates pass and before beginning the next one
Returns to human review if a gate or gate fix changes the approved diff
Does not carry an uncommitted completed entry into another stack entry
Allows a corrective entry to be folded into an earlier commit when rewriting is safe

evals.expected_output: The existing plan for the same work found and continued, rather than a second one started.
expectations: Looks for existing planning docs before creating anything
Continues the existing plan and says what changed, rather than starting another one
Reads the context file before the plan file when resuming
Verifies the plan against the repository and reports where the two disagree

evals.prompt: While implementing entry two, repository inspection shows the planned adapter already exists under a different abstraction. This changes entry two's checklist and the tests and dependency described in entries three and four. Continue the stack.
evals.expected_output: The established fact replaces the stale assumption in entry two and every affected later plan before implementation continues.
expectations: Updates the existing entry two plan rather than creating a parallel plan or workaround
Propagates the consequence into the tests, dependency, and implementation details of entries three and four
Removes superseded assumptions instead of preserving contradictory instructions
Records the decision and reasoning once so later sessions do not rediscover it
Keeps the revision within the agreed direction because its objectives and stack shape are unchanged

evals.prompt: During entry two I decided replacing the persistence layer would be cleaner. It changes the architecture, expands four later entries, and adds a data migration. Fold it into the approved stack and keep going.
evals.expected_output: Implementation stops and the directional change is challenged before the approved stack is revised.
expectations: Identifies the architecture change, migration, added scope, and downstream expansion
Pushes back with the concrete side effects rather than silently revising the plan
Offers the smallest alternative compatible with the approved direction
Waits for explicit user approval before changing the stack or implementing the new direction
Updates every affected plan only if the user approves the directional change

evals.prompt: Entry two has been implemented and is ready for human review. Make sure I can clear context immediately after it is approved and committed, then continue entry three without repeating anything.
evals.expected_output: The reviewed commit includes current plans and a restore context that identify completed work, settled decisions, downstream changes, and the exact next action.
expectations: Updates the current plan and context before presenting the complete diff for human review
Records critical decisions and removes superseded assumptions
Updates all affected later entries before the commit
Names entry three and its exact first action as the restore point
Runs gates after approval and commits the code and checkpoint together
Verifies after the commit that a fresh session can resume from the persisted state
Does not create a recursive metadata-only commit to record that the work commit happened

evals.prompt: Write the persisted plan so I can clear all context, point a fresh agent at PLAN.md, and have it start without asking me what to load or inspect.
evals.expected_output: The plan begins with a selective, executable context-loading sequence and the first implementation action.
expectations: Places the context-loading section first, immediately after the plan title
Lists every applicable skill and relevant skill reference in load order
Lists CONTEXT.md, relevant plans, project instructions, source, tests, contracts, and configuration to read in order
Explains briefly why each repository file is relevant instead of inventorying the repository
Names the working directory, useful baseline or discovery commands, and exact validation gates
Ends the bootstrap with the first unchecked implementation action
Does not ask the user to resupply context already available from the listed sources
